# Projective weighted facet credit for arbitrary endpoint faces

This note proves a weighted same-cap inequality on an actual midpoint
facet, without homothety of the endpoint faces. It also identifies an
actual two-input erosion whose first variations use precisely these
weights. It does not turn a normal-wise inequality into a global depth
bound, and it does not replace the distinct one-input continuation
weights by the weights below.

## 1. The projective weight has the required negative concavity

Fix d>=2 and delta>0. Let

 f(t)=t^(-d) for t>=delta,
 f(t)=delta^(-d)-d delta^(-d-1)(t-delta) for t<=delta.

The function f is finite, positive, decreasing and convex on R. In
addition g=f^(-1/d) is globally convex. Explicitly,

 g(t)=t for t>=delta,
 g(t)=delta[d+1-dt/delta]^(-1/d) for t<=delta.

On the lower interval

 g'(t)=[d+1-dt/delta]^(-(d+1)/d),
 g''(t)=(d+1)/delta [d+1-dt/delta]^(-(2d+1)/d)>0.

Both one-sided derivatives at delta equal one. The derivative is
therefore nondecreasing across the join, proving convexity. Consequently
every physical density w(x)=f(1+a.x) has w^(-1/d) convex, including where
its affine argument lies below delta. No positivity of that affine
argument outside the original source body is assumed.

## 2. Harmonic weighted Minkowski inequality on parallel faces

Put k=d-1. Let F_A,F_B be compact convex k-dimensional bodies in parallel
hyperplanes, and let F_K contain (F_A+F_B)/2 in the midpoint hyperplane.
Choose points c_A,c_B,y with (c_A+c_B)/2=y. Define

 w_A(x)=f(1+a.(x-c_A)),
 w_B(x)=f(1+a.(x-c_B)),
 w_K(x)=f(1+a.(x-y)),

and let the measures on these hyperplanes have those densities with
respect to their intrinsic H_k. The offsets c_A,c_B need not belong to
the faces or to their underlying bodies. Positivity and boundedness of
the weights on each compact face suffice.

For measurable convex subsets E_A subset F_A and E_B subset F_B,

 mu_K((E_A+E_B)/2) >= Harm(mu_A(E_A),mu_B(E_B)),              (1)

where Harm(s,t)=2st/(s+t) for s+t>0 and Harm(0,0)=0. A zero input mass
gives the trivial lower bound zero.

Proof. Identify the three parallel planes with the same orthonormal
tangent coordinate space. At every pair of points, Section 1 gives

 w_K((x+x')/2)^(-1/d)
   <=[w_A(x)^(-1/d)+w_B(x')^(-1/d)]/2.

Apply the functional Borell--Brascamp--Lieb inequality in dimension k
to the two restricted densities and their midpoint restricted density.
Its input exponent is p=-1/d=-1/(k+1), strictly greater than -1/k.
Its integrated exponent is p/(1+kp)=-1, exactly the harmonic mean
in (1). All functions are measurable and integrable on compact supports;
the required inequality concerns only pairs of positive input values.
It also holds for open residual subsets by the same functional statement.
This is the standard BBL theorem, not a weighted OC assertion. A precise
primary statement is Lemma 2.3 in S. Bobkov,
[Convex bodies and norms associated to convex measures](https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~bobko001/papers/2010_PTRF_Norms.pdf).
No symmetry premise is present in that functional lemma. QED.

Only (d-1)-dimensional measure is used in (1). Applying BBL in dimension
d instead would give its limiting exponent, not this harmonic inequality.

## 3. Actual ambient caps and all statuses

Place A,K,B at integer bases -1,0,1, where K contains (A+B)/2. Let u be
an active support normal with

    h_K(u)=(h_A(u)+h_B(u))/2,

and suppose its endpoint exposed faces have positive H_k measure. Take
F_A=A(u), F_B=B(u), F_K=K(u). Their midpoint inclusion is actual.
For one ORIGINAL ambient halfspace H, let U_A,U_B,U_K be the weighted
masses captured on these facets, and let a_0,b_0,m_0 be their total
weighted masses. Then

 U_K >= Harm(U_A,U_B),
 m_0-U_K >= Harm(a_0-U_A,b_0-U_B).                         (2)

For the first inequality, midpoint combinations of two captured points
are captured in the same ambient cap at the middle base. For the second,
midpoint combinations of two strictly missed points are strictly missed.
Apply (1) to the corresponding sets. Ordinary proper tangent boundaries
are H_k-null.

For a supporting coincidence, first use the exact INWARD trace convention:
an entirely coincident facet has bit one if displacement into the body
is captured, and zero otherwise. This is required for losses rather than
closed boundary profiles. Inequalities (2) remain true with these bits.
To verify this without an allocation choice, translate the three abstract
faces inward by tau v_A u, tau v_B u, and tau(v_A+v_B)u/2 for any positive
v_A,v_B. The actual affine cap-margin identity still holds. Apply (1)
to their captured and missed sets and then let tau decrease to zero.
The weights are continuous; the indicators converge almost everywhere
to the inward bits, including a whole-face coincidence. The translated
midpoint inclusion is exact, so this limit proves the assertion. These
translated abstract faces are used only to determine the correct trace,
not asserted to equal entire parallel sections of the bodies.

This also treats pure-integer caps: their bits are constant on each fiber,
and affine midpoint implication is unchanged. Taking intersections of
any specified subfamily of captured caps, or of missed caps, gives (2)
for every such joint event by the same proof. One set of physical faces
and one density enforces the whole finite cap menu; these statements do
not come from separately manufactured marginal laws.

## 4. An explicit lower bound for endpoint cap credit

Relabel the endpoints so 0<a_0<=b_0 and set R=m_0-U_K. The second
inequality in (2) implies

 U_A+U_B >= Credit(R),

 Credit(R)=a_0-R b_0/(2b_0-R) if 0<=R<2a_0b_0/(a_0+b_0),
 Credit(R)=0                 otherwise.                    (3)

The denominator in the first case is strictly positive. At its upper
endpoint the displayed expression tends to zero, so the branches join
continuously.

Proof. Write s=a_0-U_A, t=b_0-U_B, S=s+t. If S<=b_0 then
U_A+U_B>=a_0, which is stronger. Otherwise b_0<S<=a_0+b_0, and at fixed
S the minimum of st over 0<=s<=a_0, 0<=t<=b_0 occurs at an endpoint of
the interval S-b_0<=s<=a_0. The endpoint products satisfy

 b_0(S-b_0)-a_0(S-a_0)=(b_0-a_0)(S-a_0-b_0)<=0.

Hence Harm(s,t)>=2b_0(S-b_0)/S. When R<Harm(a_0,b_0), (2) implies
S<=2b_0^2/(2b_0-R), and subtracting from a_0+b_0 gives (3).
When R>=Harm(a_0,b_0), only the trivial bound is asserted. QED.

Formula (3) is the exact minimum allowed by the scalar harmonic-residual
constraint: in its positive branch take t=b_0 and
s=R b_0/(2b_0-R); in the zero branch take s=a_0,t=b_0. This scalar
sharpness does NOT claim that every equality datum is realized by a
specified original three-body geometry.

## 5. A compatible two-input erosion using these exact densities

Let y be the chosen interior source of K, a its actual projective
normalizer, and f its continued weight. Put H(n)=h_(K-y)(n)>0. Choose
any continuous bounded vector fields c_A(n),c_B(n) with
(c_A(n)+c_B(n))/2=y for every unit normal. Constant choices c_A=c_B=y
are allowed. Define

 A_e={x:n.x+e H(n) f(1+a.(x-c_A(n)))<=h_A(n) for all n},
 B_e={x:n.x+e H(n) f(1+a.(x-c_B(n)))<=h_B(n) for all n},
 K_e={x:g_(K-y)(x-y)+e f(1+a.(x-y))<=1}.                  (4)

These are nested positive convex bodies for sufficiently small e.
Each defining function is convex and continuous in its point. Uniform
boundedness of the fields on a fixed compact neighborhood, together
with an interior ball in each original input, ensures a positive
homothet remains in each intersection for small e. The chosen c_A,c_B
are not required to be interior input points.

For x in A_e,x' in B_e and m=(x+x')/2, ordinary convexity of f gives

 [f(1+a.(x-c_A(n)))+f(1+a.(x'-c_B(n)))]/2
   >=f(1+a.(m-y)).

Averaging the two input inequalities in (4) and using h_M<=h_K gives
n.m+e H(n) f(1+a.(m-y))<=h_K(n) for every n. This is exactly membership
in K_e, since the gauge is the supremum of the normalized support
inequalities. Therefore

    (A_e+B_e)/2 subset K_e                               (5)

for the ACTUAL bodies, without a common fan, a homothetic face premise,
or y in the midpoint body.

The already proved continuum-normal erosion derivative applies: its
normal speed is exactly the displayed field almost everywhere on the
boundary, and cap losses use the inward selector from Section 3. At
one active facet normal n, its three total first-loss contributions are
H(n)a_0,H(n)b_0,H(n)m_0, while its captured contributions are
H(n)U_A,H(n)U_B,H(n)U_K. Thus that facet's source-plus-input cap loss
is at least

    H(n)[U_K+Credit(m_0-U_K)],                            (6)

and its total cost is H(n)(a_0+b_0+m_0). This is an actual weighted
cap-credit inequality for arbitrary endpoint facets. Section 2 also
gives m_0>=Harm(a_0,b_0). It need not give equality or a full-volume
transport onto F_K.

## 6. Scope relative to the other continuation families

The one-input normal-allocation fields evaluate f at
((x+b_*)/2-y) or ((a_*+x')/2-y), and have the factor 2H. Their weighted
facet masses are generally DIFFERENT from a_0,b_0 here. Formula (3)
cannot be inserted with those masses without a new proof. The present
two-input family (4) is a separately feasible candidate; it can be
compared with them using its actual costs and actual same-cap losses.

Likewise (6) is not automatically stronger in every configuration than
the homothetic-facet harmonic allocation: the densities, speeds, total
costs, and midpoint-face excess differ. It removes the homothetic-face
requirement while retaining an explicit residual penalty. No assertion
that summing (6) pays Gamma_d/2, that a chosen source is deepest, or that
arbitrary many-fiber contacts can be eroded independently is made.
